I've been farming these lands in Quzhou County for over 40 years. My father taught me, and I've seen the seasons come and go. I'm 63 now, with only a primary school education, but I know this soil and this climate like I know my own hands. The North China Plain gives us two crops a year if you work it right — winter wheat followed by summer maize. That's what my neighbors do, that's what the county extension office recommends, and that's what I'll stick with. I have about 5 mu of good flat land near the well.

For wheat, I'll sow an improved variety like "Shimai 22" — I've used it before and it does well here. I'll rotary till before sowing in early October, put down compound fertilizer as basal dressing, topdress with urea at green-up, and irrigate four times: winter irrigation, jointing stage, heading, and grain filling. I'll spray herbicide once and insecticide/fungicide twice.

For summer maize, I'll plant hybrid "Denghai 605" right after the wheat harvest in early June — no-till, just plant directly into the stubble like everyone does now. I'll apply compound fertilizer at planting, irrigate twice (the summer rain helps), and spray pesticides three times. The maize grows fast and strong.

I might keep half a mu of vegetables by the house for family eating, but my main income comes from the wheat and maize rotation.
